channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, asked directly about Christian Parker’s status as defensive coordinator and if changes are being made, said “I’m not saying that.”
item.description: “I’m saying we’re still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today,” Schottenheimer concluded, notably not conclusively answering the question after the Cowboys allowed 46 points to the 49ers in what has been another lost season purely due to defensive lapses. The 34-year-old Parker was regarded as a hot coaching prospect, but the early returns have been rough. The Cowboys have allowed 282 points, the third-most in the league, and are allowing a league-worst 5.2 yards per rushing attempt.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jordan Burch (knee) will miss the remainder of the season.
item.description: Burch suffered an MCL injury in Week 10’s loss to the Rams and will now miss the remainder of the season. The second-year linebacker and former third-rounder has appeared on 235 defensive snaps this season, totaling nine pressures and one sack while earning a PFF defensive grade of 54.8. Assuming his recovery goes well, he should be in line to return in time for training camp.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending in the right direction” to practice this week.
item.description: Quinn declined to commit to opening “Bill’s” 21-day return window, but sounded optimistic about doing so later in the week. The Commanders’ RB1 has missed the last four games with a groin injury he picked up in Week 5 and would be eligible to return as early as Week 11 if he were to be designated to return this week. The Commanders have struggled on the ground without JCM this season, as their running backs have combined to average just 3.7 YPC since Week 6 while finding the end zone once. If he’s able to play against the Bengals, JCM would have some appeal as an RB3/FLEX in a week that has six teams on bye.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Chargers activated TE David Njoku from injured reserve.
item.description: Njoku will try to fight for fantasy relevancy going forward, but there’s no need to pretend he has it at the moment with all three Chargers tight ends healthy. They also activated LB Denzel Perryman off the same list and sent G/T Branson Taylor to injured reserve in their place.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers (ankle) is day-to-day.
item.description: He called the injury “significant” but “not as bad as we thought.” OK then. We would call Bowers’ status for Week 11 up in the air at this point, the practices will be guiding lights. Fantasy managers reliant on Bowers may want to look into a backup plan on this run of waivers.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik Willis (groin) is not having surgery at this time but a final decision has not been made on if he’ll have it.
item.description: “We’ll see how he feels,” Hafley said. “If he needs surgery, he will have surgery.” Well, hard to make it less complex than that. Willis is definitely out for the next three games and it sounds like there’s at least a reasonable chance he’ll be done for the season. In the meantime, Kyle McCord will play the role of bottom-five superflex starter.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said it’s too early to know if Laremy Tunsil (triceps) will return this season.
item.description: Quinn said Tunsil is progressing well in his recovery from the torn triceps he suffered in training camp and has moved on to the next phase of his recovery. Tunsil was always expected to miss all or most of the season with his injury, so it’s no surprise to hear that Quinn is unsure if he will be able to return with eight weeks left to go in the regular season. We’ll likely get more updates on his status in the coming weeks, but until the Commanders designate him for return, we can safely assume he will be out for the foreseeable future.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “that’s my plan” when asked if Micah Parsons (knee) could return in Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description: LaFleur did note that his plan has “been different than everybody else’s” throughout Parsons’ recovery, and said the star pass-rusher still has “a couple more hurdles” to clear before they can commit to him returning. Parsons has been practicing with the team since November 4th and would need to come off injured reserve by Week 12 in order to avoid being shut down for the season. With the Packers now entering their Week 11 bye, we will likely get more news on Parsons’ Week 12 status closer to the weekend.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Titans coach Robert Saleh said the Titans shifted the offensive philosophy to give Cam Ward “an opportunity” to prove he’s a franchise quarterback.
item.description: “A few weeks ago we made a shift on how we’re letting Cam Ward run the offense, let him be a field general. ... He’s looking more comfortable, his footwork is improving, and he’s doing a nice job playing quarterback. Still things he can clean up,” Saleh added. Ward over the last two weeks has four touchdown passes and his two highest passing-attempt totals of the season. We’re not exactly excited to fire up Ward as a QB1 streamer at this point, even against the Cowboys in Week 11, but given how many NFL offenses are currently trending down it’s worth pointing out that the Titans are actually taking a step forward of late.-Rivers McCown

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports George Holani (knee) has an MCL sprain and is week-to-week.
item.description: The “hope” is that Holani is not an IR candidate. His absence left Zach Charbonnet playing most of the third-down snaps yesterday, adding to his RB2 case going forward. Holani can be dropped in most leagues ahead of Seattle’s Week 11 bye.-Rivers McCown
